Mail Client

A real email client inside Odoo. Read, write and organise mail without leaving the browser tab you already work in — built first for your own mail server.

  100% Free   Open Source   LGPL-3 License   mailcow & Dovecot

Your Inbox, Not a Second Copy of It

Mirroring every message into Postgres costs you twice — once in the database, and again in every backup from then on. This one stores headers and fetches a body only when you open it.

  Mirror everything

~1.6 GB

20,000 messages at an assumed average of 80 KB, copied into Postgres whether or not anyone ever reads them.

  Headers first

~40 MB

The same 20,000 messages after a full sync: headers, flags and MIME structure, roughly 2 KB a row once indexes are counted.

How to read these numbers. Both are estimates for a 20,000-message mailbox; the first one moves with your own average message size. The 40 MB is the state right after a sync, before anything is opened — a body you read is then cached in Odoo, and a downloaded attachment is kept as well. So a mailbox in daily use sits between the two figures and grows by what you have actually read, not by everything that ever arrived.

What You Get

Three-Pane Inbox

Folders, message list and reading pane. Keyset pagination keeps a mailbox of tens of thousands responsive, with no OFFSET for the database to count past.

Real Two-Way Sync

Read, star, tag, move and delete travel back to the server through a resumable outbox. Odoo and your phone never disagree.

No User Passwords

With a Dovecot master user, one admin credential reaches every mailbox. Nobody types their mail password into Odoo.

Shared Team Mailboxes

info@, sales@ and support@ with viewer / agent / manager roles, enforced by Odoo record rules.

Tags Are IMAP Keywords

A label set in Odoo shows up in SOGo and on your phone, and labels set there show up here. Not a private list.

Attachments On Demand

Name, type and size come free from BODYSTRUCTURE. Only the part you click is ever downloaded.

See It in Action

A mail client, not a list view with an email flavour.

Folders, message list and reading pane. Every mailbox you can reach lives in one sidebar, with All Inboxes on top.

Rich composer

To, Cc and Bcc with contact autocomplete, attachments, and the </> toggle that drops you into raw HTML.

Conversations

Threaded by the RFC 5322 reference chain. The row carries a count, and the rest of the thread is linked above the message.

Quick filters

Unread, read, starred, carrying attachments, or from a known contact — on its own or on top of a search.

A self-hosted mailcow mailbox and a Gmail one, side by side — same inbox, same sync, per-mailbox unread count and connection state.

Opening a Message Should Not Cost You Anything

Email is untrusted HTML from strangers. It is treated that way.

  Tracking pixels blocked

Remote images are blocked by default — including the ones hidden in CSS backgrounds and srcset, which most blockers miss. One button loads them when you decide to.

  Sandboxed rendering

Sanitised server-side, then rendered in an iframe with neither scripting nor same-origin access.

  Credentials outside the database

Mail server passwords are encrypted with a key held in odoo.conf, so a database dump alone reveals nothing.

  Every access logged

Each mailbox opened with the master credential is recorded in an append-only log that cannot be edited or deleted from the interface.

Built for Servers You Control

Dovecot always advertises QRESYNC, CONDSTORE, MOVE and SPECIAL-USE, so the fast path is the normal path — not an optimisation that may or may not apply.

Incremental by design

QRESYNC returns changed flags and deletions in a single round trip, and UIDVALIDITY changes trigger a correct resync instead of showing stale mail.

Spam banners from Rspamd

Your antispam already scored the message. That verdict is shown as-is — no AI, no extra cost, and more accurate than either.

Push instead of polling

A token-protected endpoint lets your server trigger a sync the moment mail lands. It only accepts a trigger — never message content.

Works With

  • mailcow / Dovecot — master user or per-account passwords
  • Any IMAP server — per-account passwords
  • Gmail — OAuth2, or an app password
  • Microsoft 365 — OAuth2, or an app password

Sending reuses Odoo's own outgoing mail servers, including per-user servers, so a mailbox always sends as its own address on hosts that enforce sender identity — mailcow and Gmail both do.

Gmail and Microsoft 365 sign in with OAuth2 through Odoo's own connectors, so no password is stored. An app password works too if you prefer not to grant OAuth access.

Getting Started

1
Add the encryption key

One line in odoo.conf. Credentials are never encrypted with a key that lives in the database.

2
Connect the mail server

Host, port and how to authenticate. Test Connection reports the capabilities it found.

3
Add mailboxes

Give a mailbox an owner for a personal inbox, or leave it empty to make it a shared one.

Release Notes

What is in the box, and what is honestly not, as of the first public release.

FIRST RELEASE 19.0.1.0.0 — Odoo 19.0, LGPL-3
  Reading and organising
  • Three-pane inbox as an OWL client action, with a foldable sidebar
  • Unified All Inboxes across every mailbox you can reach
  • Conversation threading by In-Reply-To / References
  • Quick filters: unread, read, starred, has attachments, from a contact
  • Bulk mark, star, move and delete from the list
  • Tags backed by real IMAP keywords
  • Search in Odoo, or on the mail server for anything outside the sync window
  • Download the original message as .eml
  Writing
  • Composer on Odoo's html_editor, with an HTML source toggle
  • Recipient autocomplete against your contacts
  • Reply, Reply All and Forward with correct RFC 5322 threading
  • Drafts kept in Odoo and mirrored to the server's Drafts folder
  • Sent mail APPENDed to Sent, so it shows up in every other client
  • Per-mailbox signatures, optionally suppressed on replies
  Synchronisation
  • Incremental sync over QRESYNC/CONDSTORE, with a generic fallback
  • Two-way sync of flags, tags, moves and deletes through a resumable outbox
  • Correct UIDVALIDITY handling on migration or backup restore
  • Header-first storage; bodies and attachments fetched on demand
  • Token-protected push endpoint for near-instant delivery
  • Cron covers self-hosted, Gmail and Microsoft 365 mailboxes alike
  Administration and security
  • Dovecot master user, so no user password is stored in Odoo
  • Shared mailboxes with viewer / agent / manager record rules
  • Credentials encrypted with a key held in odoo.conf
  • Bodies sanitised server-side and rendered in a sandboxed iframe
  • Remote images blocked by default, CSS backgrounds included
  • Append-only audit log of every master-credential access
  • Spam banners read from existing Rspamd headers
  Known limitations in this release
  • Read-only mailboxes are read-only both ways. Under Read only sync mode, move and delete are not offered — removing a message from Odoo while it stays on the server would lose it locally for good.
  • No IMAP IDLE. New mail arrives on the cron interval, or immediately if you wire up the push URL.
  • OAuth2 for Gmail and Microsoft 365 is verified for reading and syncing. Sending over OAuth is covered by unit tests but has had less real-world exposure than the app-password route.
  • No calendar, contacts or CalDAV/CardDAV sync. This module is about mail.
  • Not an archive. It mirrors a mailbox and follows it, deletions included. For legal retention, archive at the MTA level.
  • No Chatter bridge. Logging mail against Odoo records stays Odoo's own job, deliberately.

Tested against mailcow/Dovecot and Gmail on Odoo 19.0 Community. 228 Python tests and a JavaScript suite ship with the module — run them with --test-enable --test-tags /mail_client.
